chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdillah ibn Muskhan, who said: Zakariyya ibn Malik al-Ju'fi narrated to us from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).

That he asked him about the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'And know that whatever you gain of war booty, a fifth is for Allah and the Messenger and for the near relatives and the orphans and the poor and the wayfarer.'

He said: 'As for the fifth of Allah (Mighty and Majestic), it is for the Messenger, who allocates it in the way of Allah. And as for the fifth of the Messenger, it is for his close relatives. And the fifth of the near relatives are his close relatives. And the orphans are the orphans of his Household. So He made these four [categories] as four shares for them.'
And as for the poor and the wayfarer, you know that we do not eat the charity (sadaqah) and it is not permissible for us, so it is for the poor and the sons of the wayfarer.'

key_terms.الصَّدَقَةُ: Charity, which the Imams do not consume, distinguishing it from khums
key_terms.الْيَتَامَى: The orphans, specifically the orphans of the Ahl al-Bayt in this context
key_terms.خُمُسُ اللَّهِ: The fifth of Allah, referring to the portion allocated by the Imam for public interests
key_terms.خُمْسُ الرَّسُولِ: The fifth of the Messenger, referring to the portion for the Prophet's or Imam's personal use
key_terms.ذُو الْقُرْبَى: The near relatives, specifically referring to the Banu Hashim and Banu al-Muttalib

ai.seo_question: How is the five-fold division of Khums distributed according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the Shia interpretation of Surah Al-Anfal 8:41, distinguishing between the four shares allocated to the Ahl al-Bayt and the two shares for the general Muslim community. It establishes the theological principle that the 'orphans' and 'poor' in this verse specifically refer to the Prophet's lineage, while the 'poor' and 'wayfarer' (Sadaqah) are distinct from the Imams' personal consumption, as they are prohibited from eating Sadaqah. This distinction underscores the unique status of the Ahl al-Bayt as both recipients of divine wealth and distributors of charity.
